research_mode: official ONS, MHCLG, Police.uk and HMICFRS web sources only; boundary versioning, postcode and UPRN allocation, operational-data exclusion, inspection-cycle comparability and source-snapshot guards; no parcel result or safety score claimed

sources.publisher: Police.uk / Single Online Home National Digital Team
sources.name: Police force and neighbourhood boundary downloads
verified_claims: the page publishes KML files for police force and neighbourhood policing team boundaries
force boundaries are described as constant while NPT boundaries may change monthly for operational reasons
monthly files are published with recorded checksums
limitations: police boundaries are operational policing geographies rather than ONS LSOA boundaries
a neighbourhood boundary must be month-pinned and checksum-verified before contextual use

sources.publisher: Police.uk / Single Online Home National Digital Team
sources.name: Stop and searches by force API contract
verified_claims: force stop-and-search requests accept a force identifier and optional YYYY-MM month
the latest month is returned by default even when that force has no data in that month
the documentation instructs users to use the availability endpoint when the date matters
locations are approximate rather than exact
limitations: an empty default-month response is not proof of zero activity
stop and search measures police activity and cannot be converted into parcel crime incidence

sources.publisher: Police.uk / Single Online Home National Digital Team
sources.name: Neighbourhood priorities API contract
verified_claims: the endpoint returns neighbourhood priority issues, actions and associated dates
the content is operational narrative supplied for a force-specific neighbourhood
limitations: priority narratives are not standardised crime counts or official statistics
their presence or absence cannot determine parcel safety

sources.publisher: Police.uk / Single Online Home National Digital Team
sources.name: Neighbourhood events API contract
verified_claims: the endpoint returns neighbourhood event titles, descriptions, addresses, types and ISO start and end dates
events are associated with a force-specific neighbourhood
limitations: scheduled engagement or prevention events are not crime incidents
event addresses and descriptions must not be used as parcel risk evidence

sources.publisher: Police.uk / Single Online Home National Digital Team
sources.name: Neighbourhood team API contract
verified_claims: the endpoint returns neighbourhood team member names, ranks, biographies and available contact details
limitations: team size, rank mix or missing biographies are not crime or safety measures
personnel metadata must not influence candidate scoring

sources.name: Postal geographies and limitations
verified_claims: postcode boundaries commonly do not align with administrative or statistical boundaries
centroid allocation can place some addresses in the other area when a postcode straddles a boundary
postcodes change continuously and may be reused in a different place after two years
limitations: a postcode match is not an exact property-to-LSOA assignment
postcode edition and termination status must be pinned to avoid geographic misallocation

sources.name: ONS postcode products
verified_claims: NSPL assigns postcodes to Output Areas and then higher geographies by Census-population best fit
ONSPD links current and terminated postcodes using point-in-polygon geography relationships
boundary-straddling postcodes are assigned using the mean grid reference of their addresses
postcode products are released quarterly in February, May, August and November
limitations: NSPL and ONSPD allocation methods are not interchangeable
postcode-level allocation remains less precise than address or parcel point assignment

sources.name: National Statistics UPRN Products
verified_claims: NSUL assigns an address to an Output Area by UPRN point-in-polygon and then references higher geographies by best fit
ONSUD directly allocates UPRNs to administrative, health and other geographies using the UPRN grid reference and point-in-polygon
both products are released every six weeks
limitations: NSUL and ONSUD produce different relationship types and must be selected explicitly
both depend on address products and do not prove that the runtime parcel points were joined

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: English indices of deprivation 2025 research report
verified_claims: the report provides guidance on using and interpreting IoD25
it explains higher-geography summary statistics and gives worked interpretation examples
it includes advice on interpreting change over time
limitations: higher-geography summaries are not parcel observations
change in rank or decile cannot be interpreted as absolute change without the report's caveats

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: English indices of deprivation 2025 statistical release comparability guidance
verified_claims: IoD25 uses new datasets, methodologies and geographies and is less directly comparable with earlier Indices
the release permits relative area comparison but says the Indices cannot measure absolute change over time
decile movement may reflect geography, administrative boundary, data, processing or method changes
limitations: cross-year score or rank differences cannot be presented as direct improvement or deterioration
relative deprivation is not a cardinal safety probability

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: English indices of deprivation 2025 data and spatial resources
verified_claims: the release provides spatial geopackages and mapping resources for IoD25
the page records a 17 November 2025 correction and republication of the LSOA-to-LAD lookup
Files 1 to 9 were republished as corrected v2 workbooks
limitations: only the corrected lookup and v2 resources are acceptable for joins
availability of a spatial package is not evidence that the runtime intersection succeeded

sources.name: Census geography and Output Area design
verified_claims: Output Areas were designed for similar population sizes and social homogeneity where possible
urban and rural mixes were avoided where possible and obvious boundaries were used
minimum size requirements protect confidentiality
postcodes straddling boundaries can be split across Output Areas
limitations: Output Area design principles do not establish parcel-level similarity
OA construction and postcode allocation rules must not be confused with exact parcel geometry

sources.publisher: His Majesty's Inspectorate of Constabulary and Fire & Rescue Services
sources.name: What is PEEL?
verified_claims: PEEL assesses all 43 police forces in England and Wales
assessment questions change between cycles to reflect priorities and circumstances
the site separates current and previous inspection cycles and methodologies
limitations: inspection grades are force-level assessments rather than parcel safety observations
grades from materially different cycles must not be compared as a simple time series

sources.publisher: His Majesty's Inspectorate of Constabulary and Fire & Rescue Services
sources.name: PEEL victim service and crime-recording assessment methodology
verified_claims: victim service assessments track a victim journey from report through outcome
crime-recording testing is scheduled so every force is assessed at least every three years
the report notes that British Transport Police is outside the PEEL inspection scope and that aggregated totals may differ from Home Office publications
limitations: inspection evidence is periodic and sample-based rather than continuous monthly assurance
force-level inspection findings cannot supply parcel confidence
